title: Re-evaluating Automatic LLM System Ranking for Alignment with Human Preference

live_model.evidence: "we can easily build an effective automatic bencher using GPT-4-turbo as the evaluation model, achieving a Spearman's rho of over 0.90"; Table 2 row "gpt-4-turbo 0.9112 1 0.9381 2" (Alpaca Eval / Arena Hard rho, base pairwise + Bradley-Terry); footnote resolves gpt-4-turbo to gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09

prompt.location: Appendix (pairwise/pointwise judge prompt templates, e.g. line "You are a helpful assistant in evaluating the quality of the outputs...")
prompt.note: Meta-evaluation of automatic 'benchers': the live model scores/ranks 18 candidate systems' outputs on the Alpaca Eval and Arena Hard input sets, correlated against Chatbot Arena human rankings.

claim.metric: Spearman's rho with Chatbot Arena human ranking, Alpaca Eval input set, base pairwise + Bradley-Terry aggregation
claim.location: Table 2, row gpt-4-turbo, Alpaca Eval rho column; 18 systems x ~805 Alpaca Eval instructions (exact counts in Appendix C)

data.source: Alpaca Eval and Arena Hard input sets, Chatbot Arena human rankings (all public leaderboards/benchmarks)

notes: NAACL 2025 Findings. n_items is an estimate (systems x instructions for a base-pairwise-vs-reference judge design); exact per-combination call counts are in Appendix C. gpt-4o also appears in the same table but is undated in text; gpt-4-turbo is used here because it is explicitly pinned to gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 elsewhere in the paper.
